page.layout: One page of text, one column. Running head centred at top with page number at top right. Margin notes in the right margin, at lines 1 to 6 of the first paragraph. A small star mark in the right margin beside the last paragraph before the chapter heading. Chapter heading centred, then running text.

main_text.p: Sardiniam, quod praeterire nefas est, ex Melama[?] apum abfinthii pabulo mel amarum, Hera-rum ac vicleam vero ponti ob herbas noxias vi ulen-rulentumtum proferre autores non protarii tradunt: Mellismellis autem ita venenati indicia esse, si omnino non densatur, si color magis rutilus signa.est, odoralienus, sternutamenta protinus mouens, quod ponderosius innoxio, & qui ederunt si humi se abiiciunt quaerentes re-frigerationem, Plin.li.21.c.13. scriptum reliquit, vbi quoq; remedium mellis venenati venenatiaitcile[?] multum vetus e melle optimo & rutha, falsamenta[?] etiam crebro sumta.
Hactenus de varius cibis & alimentis ad vitam prorogandam conferuandamque ne-*ceflariis[?].
main_text.head: CAP. XXI. De Condimentis.
main_text.p: Optimum cibi condimentum esse famem, potionis sitim, Cicero l.1.de finibus scribit: Et certe melius habent, qui ita simpliciter cibos suos condiunt, quam qui saccharo, pipere vel garyo-phyllis, sine quibus millia gentium eleganter & feliciter vixerunt ac etiamnunc de-gunt. Sunt enim Condimenta aliud nihil.

page.notes: Marginal notes read from the scan: "Melama[?]", "rum ac vi", "rulentum", "Mellis", "venenati", "signa." are set in italics and the first and second are uncertain. A small star mark stands in the right margin beside "ne-" and is transcribed as a note. The initial O of "Optimum" is a drawn letter and is read from the word that follows it. "ceflariis[?]" and "falsamenta[?]" and "aitcile[?]" are doubtful readings. "Melama" and "rum ac vi" are not confirmed.
